title: Meta and BlackRock form $14 billion venture for 1-gigawatt El Paso AI campus
excerpt: BlackRock-managed funds will own 80% of the project, while Meta takes the entire campus under lease agreements and secures dedicated power for its AI expansi...
content_html:
Meta (NASDAQ: META) and BlackRock (NYSE: BLK) formed a venture Tuesday to build and own a 1-gigawatt data center campus in El Paso, Texas, with estimated costs of about $14 billion. The site is already being built and is expected to start coming online in 2028.

Funds managed by BlackRock will own 80% of the venture, while Meta will retain 20% and serve as the initial sole occupant. Meta will lease the entire campus and provide construction management and property services.

Meta said the project is expected to back more than 4,000 construction jobs at the height of work, and more than 2,300 workers are already onsite. The completed campus is expected to have 300 operational jobs.

BlackRock supplies capital for Meta's buildout

Meta and BlackRock have pledged to pay their proportional shares of the estimated $14 billion development cost, covering the buildings and the long-term infrastructure that supports them. When the deal closes, Meta will add land and construction-in-progress assets worth about $2.3 billion, while BlackRock will provide roughly $4.9 billion in cash.

Meta will get a one-time payout of roughly $1 billion so the contributions match the venture's 80/20 ownership split. The structure leaves BlackRock-managed funds with the larger economic stake, while Meta runs the campus and leases all available capacity.

Part of BlackRock's investment is funded through $12.5 billion in debt. Bloomberg reported Monday that JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley arranged the bond sale through a holding company tied to BlackRock's stake in the project.

The offering attracted as much as $20 billion in orders, or about 1.6 times the amount sold, according to The Business Times, citing Bloomberg. The structure places long-dated debt at the project vehicle, with Meta's lease commitments supporting repayment rather than the borrowing sitting directly on Meta's balance sheet.

Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg tied the partnership to the scale and speed required for the company's AI plans.

"Building the infrastructure for superintelligence is key to making sure the benefits of this technology are distributed to everyone," Zuckerberg said in the announcement. "Our partnership with Larry and the team at BlackRock allows us to move faster and at greater scale."

The campus requires dedicated generation

The 1-gigawatt campus highlights the electricity demands of Meta's AI expansion. El Paso Electric is seeking approval for a 366-megawatt natural-gas facility containing 813 modular generators next to the site.

content_html_zh:
Meta（纳斯达克股票代码：META）和贝莱德（纽约证券交易所股票代码：BLK）周二成立了一家合资企业，将在德克萨斯州埃尔帕索建设并拥有一个 1 吉瓦的数据中心园区，预计成本约为 140 亿美元。 该网站已经建成，预计将于 2028 年开始上线。

贝莱德管理的基金将拥有该合资企业 80% 的股份，而 Meta 将保留 20% 的股份，并作为最初的唯一占有者。 Meta将租赁整个园区并提供建设管理和物业服务。

Meta表示，该项目预计在施工高峰期将支持超过4,000个建筑工作岗位，目前已有超过2,300名工人在现场。 竣工后的园区预计将提供 300 个运营岗位。

贝莱德为 Meta 的扩建提供资金

Meta 和 BlackRock 已承诺按比例支付估计 140 亿美元的开发成本，涵盖建筑物和支持它们的长期基础设施。 交易完成后，Meta 将增加价值约 23 亿美元的土地和在建资产，而贝莱德将提供约 49 亿美元的现金。

Meta 将获得约 10 亿美元的一次性支付，因此出资额与该合资企业 80/20 的所有权分配相匹配。 这种结构使贝莱德管理的基金拥有更大的经济股份，而 Meta 则负责运营园区并租赁所有可用容量。

贝莱德的部分投资是通过 125 亿美元的债务筹集的。 彭博社周一报道称，摩根大通和摩根士丹利通过一家与贝莱德在该项目中持有股份相关的控股公司安排了债券销售。

据《商业时报》援引彭博社报道，此次发行吸引了高达 200 亿美元的订单，约为销售额的 1.6 倍。 该结构将长期债务置于项目工具上，Meta 的租赁承诺支持偿还，而不是直接在 Meta 的资产负债表上借款。

Meta 创始人兼首席执行官马克·扎克伯格将合作伙伴关系与公司人工智能计划所需的规模和速度联系在一起。

扎克伯格在声明中表示：“构建超级智能基础设施是确保每个人都能享受到这项技术的好处的关键。” “我们与拉里和贝莱德团队的合作使我们能够更快、更大规模地采取行动。”

校园需要一代人的奉献

1 吉瓦园区凸显了 Meta 人工智能扩展的电力需求。 埃尔帕索电力公司 (El Paso Electric) 正在寻求批准在该地点附近建设一座 366 兆瓦的天然气设施，其中包含 813 台模块化发电机。
